clue.text: This fuss not half bad — get a quick look

indicators.note: something bad is spoilt or messed up, so the letters are put into a new order
only the front half of the word fuss is kept, giving its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a minor fuss as not too bad and takes a quick glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges THIS plus FU (half of fuss). 'Not half bad' reads as the idiom for 'quite good', which hides the halving.
explanation.definitionFit: A shufti is British slang, from army Arabic, for a brief glance or peek.

clue.text: Immoral woman in group entertaining president

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a set is a group of things
Donald Trump, US president

explanation.surface: A disreputable woman in a gathering that is playing host to the president.
explanation.definitionFit: A strumpet is an old-fashioned insulting word for a promiscuous woman or prostitute.

clue.text: Man of the match

parts.note: the sporting award phrase, reread with match as a marriage: the man getting married

explanation.definitionFit: A wedding is a match between two people, and the male partner marrying is the man at its centre.

clue.text: Significant time seen as divine always

parts.note: a divine is a theologian; DD is Doctor of Divinity
ay (or aye) is an old word meaning ever or always

explanation.surface: A notable moment seen as godly and permanent.
explanation.definitionFit: D-Day was the Allied landing date of 1944, and the term now names any decisive or crucial date.

clue.text: One leading soldiers in skilful operation that could go wrong?

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed in the middle of the other word

parts.note: expert means skilled

indicators.note: one goes ahead of the soldiers, so I comes before MEN

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
men is a common word for soldiers

explanation.surface: An officer leads troops in a clever military operation that might fail.
explanation.definitionFit: An experiment is a trial procedure whose outcome is uncertain, so it may well fail.

clue.text: Female graduate taking on a learner

indicators.note: the graduate takes on extra letters, which go at the front of MA

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate letter
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A woman graduate takes on a trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma is a woman's given name, so it stands for a female person.

clue.text: Fly as ace through start of thunderstorm and escape finally

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in playing cards
via means by way of, through

indicators.note: the opening letter of thunderstorm is taken
the closing letter of escape is taken

explanation.surface: A flying ace pilots through a storm and gets away at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To aviate is to pilot an aircraft, a formal verb for flying.

clue.text: Fool to rush in — one giving agreement

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to rush in is to enter

explanation.surface: Echoes the saying that fools rush in, with someone nodding along.
explanation.definitionFit: An assenter is a person who consents or agrees, from the verb assent.

clue.text: Dissident there, nasty old party getting cross

indicators.note: something nasty is in a bad state, so these letters are messed up and reordered

parts.note: a do is a party
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A rebel over there, from some unpleasant old political party, is angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges THERE as HETER. 'Party' looks political but is a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Heterodox describes views departing from accepted doctrine, as a dissident's do.

clue.text: Biographies giving false accounts about victor

indicators.note: the first word goes about, around, the other letter

parts.note: lies are untrue accounts
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Life stories that misrepresent a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A biography is a written life, so a collection of them are lives.

clue.text: Factory set up by railway

indicators.note: next to: the railway letters sit beside the other word

parts.note: to found something is to set it up

explanation.surface: A factory established by a railway company.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundry is a works where metal is cast, a kind of industrial plant.

clue.text: Ultimately, indecisive fellow had to come out

indicators.note: in the end, so the final letter of indecisive is taken

parts.note: a man is a fellow
had a meal: ate

explanation.surface: A dithering man eventually had to reveal himself.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source.

clue.text: One fairly quiet little rascal

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
mp, mezzo piano, is the musical direction for moderately soft

explanation.surface: A mischievous child who is, for once, reasonably quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a small devil, and so a mischievous child.

clue.text: Men trashing unusual decoration

indicators.note: out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Men wrecking some odd ornamentation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trashing' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'unusual' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnishment is an embellishment or adornment, as a garnish decorates food.

clue.text: Growing tendency to take endless chance with stupid dieting

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a risk is a chance

indicators.note: stupid suggests muddled thinking, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rising trend for taking risks with foolish diets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts RISK to RIS; 'stupid' rearranges DIETING as INGTIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising tide is used figuratively for a strengthening trend or movement.

clue.text: Hold husband, having fallen out with boy

indicators.note: put out of order, so the letters of fallen are rearranged

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A husband who has quarrelled with his son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges FALLEN as ALFNEL; 'fallen out' reads as having quarrelled.
explanation.definitionFit: A half nelson is a wrestling grip, one arm locked behind the opponent's neck.

clue.text: Get drunk after initial loss in gambling game

indicators.note: once its first letter is lost, the synonym is shortened at the front

parts.note: blotto is slang for very drunk

explanation.surface: Someone drinks heavily after early losses at the tables.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery-style game of chance played for money.

clue.text: Beautiful woman in hat verbally abused

indicators.note: the woman goes in the hat

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A lovely woman in a hat is insulted.
explanation.definitionFit: To libel someone is to defame them; strictly in writing, here loosely in words.

clue.text: Discover Durham, say

definitions.meaning: Durham is a bishopric, a bishop's seat or diocese

explanation.definitionFit: A see is the area of a bishop's authority, and to see something is to discover it.

clue.text: Start to like maiden, maybe — hoping she will become this?

indicators.note: the opening letter of like is taken

parts.note: a maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored

explanation.surface: Starting to fancy a young woman, hoping she will become a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled, and a maiden over is one with no runs off it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone smitten hopes the woman will become a romantic partner, a sweetheart.

clue.text: Servant about 50 leads cheers in the capital

indicators.note: comes first, so the servant piece is placed before the thanks
the servant goes about, around, the numeral

parts.note: a valet is a manservant
L is the Roman numeral for 50
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A servant aged about fifty leads the toasts in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Valletta is the capital city of Malta, so it fits a clue naming just a capital.

clue.text: Ruddy fashionable people in Indianan city

parts.note: ruddy and blooming are both mild British intensifiers, and both mean rosy
the ton is high society

explanation.surface: Mock outrage at trendy folk in an Indiana city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomington is a city in Indiana, home of Indiana University.

clue.text: Food associated with chips in Carroll's story

definitions.text: Food associated with chips in Carroll's story

parts.words: Food associated with chips in Carroll's story
parts.note: in Lewis Carroll's poem The Walrus and the Carpenter, shellfish are eaten; chips suggests fish and chips

explanation.definitionFit: The shellfish eaten by the Walrus and the Carpenter in Through the Looking-Glass are these bivalves.

clue.text: Girl turning around creates delay

indicators.note: turned to face the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: gal is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl who turns back holds things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A lag is a gap or interval in time, a delay.

clue.text: A drug's bamboozled prison officers perhaps

indicators.note: fooled and confused, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A narcotic has fooled the warders.
explanation.definitionFit: Prison warders are one example of guards, those who watch over others.

clue.text: Attack the French and yell

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)
to shout is to yell

explanation.surface: An order to attack the French with a yell.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out is to strike or speak at someone suddenly and violently.

clue.text: A time to tuck into extra-large breakfast dish?

indicators.note: to tuck into is to go inside, so the letters go within the size label

parts.note: OS is outsize, the clothing label for extra-large

explanation.surface: Time for a hearty breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' reads as eating heartily. The question mark flags that the grain itself is not a dish until cooked as porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are cooked into porridge, a classic breakfast food.

clue.text: A flaming resinous material flowing round hole produced by explosion

indicators.note: the run of letters flows back round the other way, so they are read backwards

parts.note: flaming red, the colour of fire
lac is a resinous insect secretion used for shellac

explanation.surface: Molten resin pouring around a blast hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing round' reverses the whole run of pieces; 'flaming' and 'flowing' paint lava, but neither is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A caldera is a large volcanic crater, formed when an eruption blows out or collapses a summit.

clue.text: US singer making money

explanation.definitionFit: Johnny Cash was an American country star, and cash is ready money.

clue.text: Always No. 1 in tennis? No, but she did win Wimbledon!

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: the number one, first, letter of tennis

explanation.surface: Was she always tennis's top player? No, but she did win Wimbledon.
explanation.definitionFit: Chris Evert, US tennis player, won the Wimbledon singles three times.

clue.text: Girl's wrong and boy is twisted

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so Di's
a tort is a civil wrong in law
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl has gone wrong and a boy is warped.
explanation.definitionFit: Distorted means bent out of shape or misrepresented, as something twisted is.
